name: GSK2881078

lead: GSK2881078 is a non-steroidal SARM from GlaxoSmithKline, built for muscle weakness in chronic and acute illness. Muscle-focused readers cite it as one of the better human data sets for a SARM.

It acts on the androgen receptor to promote muscle growth and has a very long half-life, reported at over 100 hours. In healthy older adults it produced dose-dependent lean mass gains over placebo, and in a 13-week trial in men with COPD it increased leg strength beyond exercise alone, though patient-reported outcomes did not change. Trials were in older or ill people, not people seeking a cosmetic physique.

paras: It was given in clinical trials, often alongside an exercise program in the COPD study. It is not a marketed product.

Trials reported lowered HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, transient ALT liver-enzyme elevations and, in one case, a drug rash. It is not approved, and SARM safety reviews cite liver injury and tendon rupture cases with recreational SARM use.

chain: Gain in lean mass and leg strength
angle.text: GSK2881078 is a SARM that activates the androgen receptor and raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, so muscle-focused readers cite it as a human data set. Trials were in ill or older people rather than people seeking a cosmetic physique.

lead: GSK2881078 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by GlaxoSmithKline for muscle weakness associated with chronic and acute illness.[1] It has been tested in phase 1 and phase 2 trials, including studies in healthy older adults and in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).[1][2][3]

Trials found dose-dependent increases in lean mass, and in men with COPD a gain in leg strength beyond exercise alone.[1][3] Reported safety findings included reductions in HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, and transient rises in liver enzyme (ALT) levels.[2][3][1] It is not approved for any use.

paras: GSK2881078 is of interest to people who want more muscle because it activates the androgen receptor selectively in muscle, and in trials it raised lean body mass in older adults; more lean mass is the first step in a chain toward a fuller, stronger physique.[1][4] The compound was developed for people with muscle weakness from illness, however, and its human trials enrolled older adults and people with COPD rather than young lifters.[1][3]

A 2025 systematic review of SARMs and physical performance covering nine studies and 970 patients (mean age 57.1 years) included GSK2881078 among six compounds examined for lean mass, fat mass, stair-climbing power and leg-press strength.[4]

Selective androgen receptor modulators are non-steroidal compounds intended to produce the muscle-building effects of androgens while limiting effects on other tissues. Reviews describe them as candidates for sarcopenia, cachexia and frailty, with enobosarm and GSK2881078 among the compounds in clinical trials.[5] A 2026 review of sarcopenia lists GSK2881078 alongside enobosarm and myostatin-neutralizing antibodies as emerging therapies showing dose-dependent gains in appendicular lean mass.[6]

In healthy older men and women, repeat dosing produced greater lean mass accrual than placebo at all dose levels, with women responding at lower doses than men.[1] In the COPD trial, leg strength rose in men and the lean mass increased, but patient-reported outcomes did not change.[3] A 2025 systematic review of randomized trials assessed SARMs and physical performance across compounds.[4]

The first-in-human study reported a dose-related lowering of HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, mostly mild drug-related adverse events, one drug rash leading to withdrawal, and two cases of elevated creatine phosphokinase after exertion.[2] The phase 1b study reported no serious adverse events but transient ALT elevations.[1] The COPD trial reported reversible HDL-cholesterol reductions and transient transaminase elevations as the main treatment-related findings.[3] A 2023 systematic review of SARM safety in healthy adults, written with recreational users in mind, notes case reports of drug-induced liver injury and tendon rupture with SARMs and that obtaining them for personal use is illegal in the US.[7]

The 2023 systematic review of SARM safety in healthy adults covered 33 reports, including 18 trials and 15 case reports or series, with case reports of drug-induced liver injury, an Achilles tendon rupture and rhabdomyolysis; it reports that two individuals exposed to GSK2881078 in a clinical trial had rhabdomyolysis, and that ALT elevations averaged 7.1 percent across SARM trials.[7] Its authors conclude that recreational use should be strongly discouraged and that obtaining SARMs for personal use is illegal in the US.[7]

The first-in-human study found dose-proportional exposure and a half-life above 100 hours.[2] A cohort in the phase 1b study found that inhibiting the enzyme CYP3A4 was unlikely to alter its pharmacokinetics in a clinically significant way.[1] Comparative in vitro work has examined it alongside RAD-140 and GLPG0492.[8]

Three human studies are summarized here. (1) A first-in-human study in healthy men and postmenopausal women of single and 7 to 14 day repeat doses (NCT02045940).[2][9] (2) A phase 1b randomized placebo-controlled study in healthy older men and postmenopausal women dosed for up to about 8 weeks, which found dose-dependent lean mass increases and transient ALT elevations (NCT02567773).[1][10] (3) A 13-week phase 2A randomized trial in 97 people with COPD (47 postmenopausal women, 50 men) combined with a home exercise programme; leg strength increased in men (difference from placebo of about 7 percent, 90% CI 0.5 to 13.6), with a non-significant trend in women (NCT03359473).[3][11]

Analytical laboratories have published methods to detect GSK2881078 and its metabolites in urine and hair after a single oral dose, and in equine samples, as part of anti-doping work.[12][13][14] Specific use of this compound in looksmaxxing communities is not documented.

Doping-control researchers have developed urine, hair and equine metabolite methods for GSK2881078, and the compound is among the SARMs covered by multi-class liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry screening.[12][13][14] An interview study with COPD patients in the phase 2 program documented patient perspectives on disease experience and trial participation.[6]
